author: karapatan
title: Primer on Desaparecidos
content: ANG SAPILITANG PAGKAWALA O ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE ay isa sa pinakamalubhang paglabag sa karapatang pantao. Hindi ito simpleng pagkawala ng tao – ito ay sistematikong pagdukot, pagpapahirap at pagtatago sa isang indibidwal, na isinasagawa ng mga ahente ng gobyerno o mga grupong kumikilos na may basbas ng gobyerno. Layunin nitong patahimikin ang biktima, pigilan ang kanyang adbokasiya, at maghasik ng takot sa kanyang pamilya at mas malawak na mamamayan.

author: karapatan
title: Contribution to the 2026 International Ecumenical Peace Convocation Seoul, Republic of Korea
content:
Contribution to the 2026 International Ecumenical Peace Convocation Seoul, Republic of Korea 09 September 2026

Cristina Palabay KARAPATAN Secretary General

Good day to everyone, and thank you for having us in the panel.

The Philippines is in a seemingly chronic state of crisis as far as human and people’s rights are concerned. The violations of human rights and international humanitarian law are systematic and systemic, which means that these are deliberate acts, which were planned methodically, instigated and funded by State authorities and actors, and that these are borne out of a system that breeds and maintains injustice, despite the Philippine government’s accession or ratification of almost all international covenants on human rights.

From the Marcos dictatorship in the 1970’s to the current Marcos the son’s administration, government campaigns pertaining to the most-often used bywords of “national security,” “peace and order,” “peace and development,” “human security,” and others have been used to justify and legitimize the gravest atrocities and the most brutal and inhumane crimes against humanity.

Filipinos are still reeling from the sham drug war of former President Rodrigo Duterte which resulted in the mass murder of more than 30,000 citizens accused of peddling or using drugs, including more than 300 children and minors who were considered “collateral damage.”

author: karapatan
title: Karapatan Monitor for April to June 2026
content:
On April 19, 2026, ten guerrillas of the New People’s Army (NPA) and nine civilians were massacred by troops of the 79th Infantry Battalion of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (IBPA) in Barangay Salamanca, Toboso, Negros Occidental.

The gruesome incident bore all signs of a war crime. A drone footage of Roger Fabillar, an NPA leader who was purportedly captured alive, which circulated online contradicting the AFP’s official line that he was killed in action. In violation of international humanitarian law (IHL), the military used disproportionate and excessive force, failed to undertake measures to avoid or minimize deaths, did not take steps to distinguish armed combatants from unarmed civilians, imposed a day-long media black-out and issued suspiciously conflicting reports on the places of incidence and the number of recovered firearms. The AFP was obviously intent on taking control of the narrative in order to cover up one of the Marcos Jr. regime’s most horrific war crimes to date.

The massacre of the Negros 19 soon dominated the news and galvanized outrage against the intensified military operations in the countryside. On May 21, 2026, the results of a National Fact-Finding and Solidarity Mission (NFFSM) joined by more than a hundred individuals representing various organizations confirmed earlier reports that nine of the 19 massacre victims were civilians.
